10.2b — ScriptableObjects: Card Data as Assets

Yesterday's deck is a list of... what? Today: the CARD itself — as a ScriptableObject, Unity's trick for making DATA feel like an asset you drag. After today, adding a card to your game means clicking, not coding — your jam gets a content pipeline.

Concept Lab ~15 min

The ScriptableObject, defined. It is a data class that becomes a FILE in your project (an asset, like a sprite). Each instance is one card, editable in the Inspector:

[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "Cards/New Card")]
public class Card : ScriptableObject
{
    public string cardName;
    public Sprite art;
    public int cost;
    public int attack;
    public int defense;
    public string description;
}

Right-click in Assets → Create → Cards → New Card — and an .asset file appears. Make FIVE cards. Open them in the Inspector: fields, not code. Designers edit these; programmers only build the shape once.

Compare your three data homes so far:

Data lives in…Example you builtEdited by
Serialized fields on a componentturret's maxAttackRange (3.1)Inspector, per scene object
Scene/prefab YAMLeverything (9.4)Unity (and you, by hand, once)
ScriptableObject assetsyour cardsInspector, in the PROJECT, reusable everywhere

Socratic

The starter's six Lists hold these Card objects. When you APPEND the same asset reference into three different hands, how many COPIES of the card exist in memory — and why is "reference, not copy" exactly what 9.4 guids do for sprites? (One card asset, many references. The exam's word is abstraction — again.)

Build Lab ~30 min

Step 1 — build the card script above (check whether your starter already has a Card.cs — some versions ship one; if so, READ it and extend with a field of your own: effect text, rarity, flavor).

Step 2 — the deck in the Inspector. In GameManager, the deck can be authored directly:

[SerializeField] private List<Card> startingDeck; // drag cards in!

Drag your five (then fifteen) card assets into the list in the Inspector. Duplicate entries are legal — three copies of your best card IS a design decision.

Step 3 — prove the pipeline. Add a card WITHOUT touching any code: create, fill, drag into deck, play. If that took under two minutes, your content pipeline works. The jam's remaining days are this pipeline plus the EMPTY methods (10.2c).

Bug Hunt: Data design traps

  1. Your Card has 12 fields and five use none. Which fields earn their place — and what does the exam call the discipline of matching data to use (5.1: right-size the data)?
  2. You EDIT a card asset during Play mode. Press stop. What survived — and why is asset data MORE dangerous to edit than scene data at runtime?
  3. Two cards share one art sprite. You delete the sprite file. What did 9.4 teach you happens — and how many cards broke?
Close of Day ~5 min

Tinker: Deck design

  1. Author your full 15–20 card deck as assets. Write a one-sentence balance note per card ("cheap but weak"). Tomorrow you SHUFFLE this labor of love.
  2. Commit + push: "10.2b: card assets + authored deck".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain a ScriptableObject vs a component vs a prefab
  • Create, edit, and reference card assets in a list
  • Explain references vs copies when one asset sits in three lists
  • Add a card with zero code changes (the pipeline test)
